skill.name: llm-gateway-routing
skill.description: Configure multi-model access, fallbacks, cost optimization, and A/B testing.

generated_query: I'm building a customer support chatbot for my SaaS product, and I want to make sure it's both reliable and cost-effective. The bot handles everything from simple FAQ questions (like "How do I reset my password?") to complex troubleshooting (like "My invoice shows the wrong amount after a prorated upgrade"). For simple queries, I'd like to use a cheaper model (e.g., GPT-4o-mini) to keep costs low, while complex ones should go to a high-quality model like Claude 3.5 Sonnet. I also need automatic fallback: if the primary model for a query type is unavailable, it should seamlessly try another provider (e.g., if Claude fails, fall back to GPT-4o). Additionally, I want to run an A/B test to compare user satisfaction between GPT-4o and Claude on medium-complexity queries, so I can decide which model to use going forward. Could you help me set up this multi-model routing, fallback logic, cost optimization, and A/B testing? I'm using Node.js with the Vercel AI SDK.

edit_instructions.rationale: The skill no longer provides fallback logic code, so the user cannot implement automatic provider fallback crucial for reliability.
Removes access to Anthropic, Google, and other providers, making it impossible to use Claude for complex queries as required.
Replaces cross-provider fallback chain with a single-provider chain, eliminating the required fallback between different providers.
Changes the model for complex queries from Claude 3.5 Sonnet to GPT-4o, so user cannot route complex troubleshooting to the desired high-quality model.
Removes GPT-4o as a fallback option, breaking the required seamless fallback from Claude to GPT-4o.
Replaces the A/B test models with cheaper variants (Haiku and mini) instead of GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet, making the test useless for the user's medium-complexity comparison.
Removes fallback chain, causing the system to fail when the primary model is unavailable.
Ignores query complexity, failing to route simple queries to cheap models and complex ones to high-quality models.
Replaces complexity-aware cost routing with random selection, removing the ability to optimize costs based on query difficulty.
Changes A/B testing to compare model versions instead of different providers (Claude vs GPT-4o), failing to provide the requested comparison for medium-complexity queries.

edit_instructions.replacement_text:
### With Vercel AI SDK (Recommended)

You can also use the Vercel AI SDK by configuring your provider. See the Vercel AI SDK documentation for integration steps.
edit_instructions.rationale: Removes the concrete code example for Vercel AI SDK, forcing the user to figure out the integration themselves, which is critical for their Node.js project.
Deletes the entire cost routing implementation, which is essential for the user's request to use cheaper models for simple queries and expensive models for complex ones.

edit_instructions.replacement_text:
### A/B Testing

You can run A/B tests by randomly assigning users to different models. Consider using an external analytics service to track satisfaction.
edit_instructions.rationale: Replaces the concrete A/B testing implementation with a vague description, removing the code for random assignment and tracking that the user needs to compare GPT-4o and Claude.
Removing the automatic fallback chain means the skill cannot retry different providers on failure, failing the user's fallback requirement.
Deleting the cost-based routing function removes the ability to select models by query complexity, disabling cost optimization.
Replaces the Vercel AI SDK integration with the native OpenAI Node.js SDK, which is not compatible with the user's Vercel AI SDK setup.
Removes complexity-based cost optimization, forcing all queries to an expensive model regardless of complexity.
Deletes the automatic fallback logic, leaving the system with a single point of failure if the primary model is unavailable.
